Dulce et Decorum Est, by Wilfred Owen

"Bent double, like old beggars under sacks,

Knock-kneed, coughing like hags, we cursed through sludge,

Till on the haunting flares we turned our backs

And towards our distant rest began to trudge.

Men marched asleep. Many had lost their boots

But limped on, blood-shod. All went lame; all blind;

Drunk with fatigue; deaf even to the hoots

Of tired, outstripped Five-Nines that dropped behind.

Gas! GAS! Quick, boys! - An ecstasy of fumbling,

Fitting the clumsy helmets just in time;

But someone still was yelling out and stumbling

And flound'ring like a man in fire or lime ...

Dim, through the misty panes and thick green light,

As under I green sea, I saw him drowning.

In all my dreams, before my helpless sight,

He plunges at me, guttering, choking, drowning.

If in some smothering dreams you too could pace

Behind the wagon that we flung him in,

And watch the white eyes writhing in his face,

His hanging face, like a devil's sick of sin;

If you could hear, at every jolt, the blood

Come gargling from the froth-corrupted lungs,

Obscene as cancer, bitter as the cud

Of vile, incurable sores on innocent tongues, --

My friend, you would not tell with such high zest

To children ardent for some desperate glory,

The old lie: Dulce et decorum est Pro patria mori.

( "It is sweet and right to die for your country.")

Anthem for Doomed Youth

By Wilfred Owen

What passing-bells for these who die as cattle?

— Only the monstrous anger of the guns.

Only the stuttering rifles' rapid rattle

Can patter out their hasty orisons.

No mockeries now for them; no prayers nor bells;

Nor any voice of mourning save the choirs,—

The shrill, demented choirs of wailing shells;

And bugles calling for them from sad shires.

What candles may be held to speed them all?

Not in the hands of boys, but in their eyes

Shall shine the holy glimmers of goodbyes.

The pallor of girls' brows shall be their pall;

Their flowers the tenderness of patient minds,

And each slow dusk a drawing-down of blinds.

Funny thing is that when talking about politics among Russian (and other Slavic) Christians when I go to church, for the most part they are quite receptive to critiques of the police, military, government, and everything else in general. That being said, it's not like they are an-caps either but talking with them is much easier. From my experience with Americans though, I usually snake my way around. Maybe the conversation is on the war, "muh freedoms", etc - so I'll have them talk for as long they do then I just drop some food for thoughts. I usually use moral arguments with some economics put along with it as from my experience tend to be more open to that (and I'll admit I am like that too myself). Like with the Iraq War, I'll drop the idea of how we (aka gov) killed far more people than were killed on 9/11. I then raise the question on when do we reach the right amount of "payback" for what happened on 9/11. Then I go to the idea on whether it is right at all considering how much more damage the U.S. has done to that area (in the past, present, and future damages with the economy, emotional, intra-national relationships, etc). If everything goes well and they are still listening, I then go to the problems war and other things create in here the U.S. like with taxes, wasted money on the war and other things, etc. It may not change folks' beliefs and thoughts right away, but by building a pile of these thoughts, they can eventually influence folks to see things in a different light (hopefully toward libertarian/ancap thought).
